span.label: The measurement is a bulk signal, and the authors state they cannot exclude having missed intermingled subpopulations averaged out within it.
span.note: what this limits: the absence of task-relevant activity in an area of these maps: the signal is a bulk population measure and the authors state intermingled subpopulations could be averaged out within it

span.label: The grouping variable the entire result rests on is, in some sessions, assigned by a substitute measure whose accuracy is stated as 75%.
span.note: what this limits: the active/passive trial labels in this study: in sessions without usable body-camera images they were predicted from a z-axis focus drop, reported at 75% accuracy against the camera
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The independent variable is changed by the manipulation. Strategy is treated as what determines where short-term memory sits, but optogenetic silencing of the site induces strategy switches that persist across days and appear in non-perturbation trials. The paper reports this as a result rather than as a threat, and it is the correct reading - but it means strategy and site are mutually determining, not one prior to the other, and the title states only one direction.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Two thresholds on the same movement signal do different jobs: one splits trials into active and passive by movement during the sensation period, the other discards trials with movement in the first second of the delay as noisy. The grouping rule and the exclusion rule read the same measure, so which trials survive is not independent of which class they were assigned to.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: M2 —causes→ behavioral strategy
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — THE PAPER'S GROUPING VARIABLE IS NOT EXOGENOUS, AND THE PAPER IS THE ONE THAT SHOWS IT. The title says strategy DETERMINES where memory is held; silencing the area that holds it makes the animal CHANGE STRATEGY - 'some mice ... apparently flexibly SWITCH TO THE ALTERNATIVE UNPERTURBED STRATEGY', and those switches were 'consistent across days, present also in trials without perturbation and were clearly reflected in corresponding switches between M2- and P-dominated delay maps.' So the arrow runs both ways: strategy selects the site, and removing the site reselects the strategy. Recorded as `causes` in the direction the manipulation establishes, since that is the one an experiment tested.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: behavioral strategy —operationalised-as→ z-axis drop in focus
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.5 — the record marks this weak — IN A SUBSET OF SESSIONS THE VARIABLE THE WHOLE RESULT IS CONDITIONED ON WAS READ OFF AN IMAGING ARTEFACT: where the body camera failed, movement was predicted from 'the z-axis drop in focus (using a 10% drop from baseline in 3 in-focus single cells as criterion; 75% ACCURACY in labeling trials by validating with move vector from the body camera)'. The accuracy is stated, which is what makes it auditable - but a quarter of those trials carry the wrong class. Low weight for that reason.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Which cortical area held the delay-period memory depended on the mouse's behavioural strategy: persistent activity sat medio-frontally (M2) on active trials but in a lateral posterior area on passive trials.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The posterior whisker areas encoded the animal's choice soon after touch under both strategies, so the strategy difference appeared only later, during the delay.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Optogenetically silencing M2 or area P lowered task performance only in trials run with the strategy that area supports, and left the other strategy unaffected.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Silencing M2 and area P together dropped all four VGAT-ChR2 mice to performance indistinguishable from the non-expert threshold, which single-area silencing had not done.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Some mice escaped a perturbation by switching behavioural strategy rather than losing performance, one passive mouse turning active during the perturbation sessions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The two memory sites hold different content: the motor-sensory index was positive in M2 (activity grouped by the upcoming action) and negative in area P (activity grouped by the past texture).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On passive trials a classifier restricted to frontal-cortex pixels could not tell hit from correct-rejection trials at all, showing short-term memory need not reside in frontal cortex.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The more a mouse used the active strategy the better it discriminated textures, and passive mice needed roughly twice as many sessions to reach expert level.
